confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on aggregated cost-of-living figures from one web search. Those sources put a cappuccino at about $2, a 0.5 L pub beer at $4.80–5.80, an inexpensive meal at $12–16 and a mid-range dinner at about $29 per person. The sources disagree on mid-range dinner prices, so I estimated from the plausible ones. The cocktail and wine prices come from the local price relationship to beer and general knowledge, not from direct searches, so they are less certain. The accommodation prices are my own model estimates for peak-summer July 2026. I did not check any booking sites, and real prices could vary by 25% or more. The exchange rate is the RBA's 18 November 2026 rate as reported in a search summary. I did not open the RBA page itself.
comparable_city_reasoning: Palermo was treated as cheaper than the Italian average, roughly 15% below, and comparable to Naples and Bari. Prices sit below those in Rome and Florence. Accommodation is set at southern-Italian levels for the summer peak season.
